spoken_summary.summary_zh:
看世界的两种方式：有人看到想要的东西，有人只看到阻碍；伐木工的故事说明无限思维——不是每天做多少，而是一生能做多少，记得停下来磨斧头。
五条规则的第一条：直接去拿你想要的，不必排队，只要不挡住别人；第二条：像海豹突击队一样，真正通过选拔的人是那些在精疲力竭时还能帮助身边人的人。
第三条：像曼德拉一样，最后一个发言——先听所有人说，再给出自己的意见；第四条：有时问题出在你自己身上，像19世纪医生不洗手导致产褥热一样，要承担责任。
第五条：谦卑与感恩——别人对你的好是对你职位的，不是你本人的，你永远只配一个泡沫杯。
对年轻一代的共情：他们不是难懂，而是我们创造了让他们上瘾的环境；多巴胺、社交媒体、表面关系，让他们失去了应对压力的能力。
热爱工作是一种权利，不是特权；为不爱的事努力叫压力，为爱的事努力叫激情。
spoken_summary.summary_en:
Two ways to see the world: some see what they want, others see what blocks them; the lumberjack story teaches an infinite mindset—it's not about daily output but lifetime output, so stop and sharpen your axe.
Rule one: go after what you want without waiting in line, as long as you don't block others; rule two: like Navy SEALs, those who make it are the ones who help the person next to them when they have nothing left.
Rule three: be the last to speak like Nelson Mandela—listen to everyone first, then offer your opinion; rule four: sometimes you are the problem, as with 19th-century doctors who didn't wash hands, so take accountability.
Rule five: humility and gratitude—people treat you well because of your position, not you; you always deserve a styrofoam cup.
Empathy for the younger generation: they're not difficult, we've created an addictive environment; dopamine, social media, and superficial relationships leave them without coping skills.
Loving your work is a right, not a privilege; working hard for something you don't care about is stress, for something you love is passion.
script_zh: 今天我想和你聊聊看世界的两种方式。有些人看到的是自己想要的东西，有些人看到的却是挡住他们的障碍。这个区别，可能决定了你的一生。
先讲个伐木工的故事：两个人每天同时开始砍树，同时收工，但其中一个每天中午消失一小时，却总能砍更多柴。秘诀是什么？他回家磨斧头了。这就是无限思维——别只看每天做了多少，要看一生能做多少。
西蒙·斯涅克给了我们五条规则。第一，直接去拿你想要的，不用排队，只要不挡别人的路。第二，像海豹突击队那样，真正的高手是在自己精疲力竭时还能帮助身边人的人。第三，像曼德拉一样，最后一个发言，先听所有人说。
第四，有时候问题就出在你身上。19世纪的医生不洗手就接生，导致无数产妇死亡，他们却怪别人。要敢于承担责任。第五，保持谦卑和感恩——别人对你的好，是对你的职位，不是你本人，你永远只配一个泡沫杯。
我们还谈到对年轻一代的共情。他们不是难懂，而是我们创造了一个让他们上瘾的环境。社交媒体、多巴胺、表面的关系，让他们失去了应对压力的能力。热爱工作是一种权利，不是特权。为不爱的事努力叫压力，为爱的事努力叫激情。
所以，你打算怎么用这些规则？是继续排队，还是直接去拿？是最后一个发言，还是急于表达？记住，磨斧头的时间，才是你真正成长的时间。
script_en: Today I want to talk about two ways of seeing the world. Some people see the thing they want, and some people see the thing that prevents them from getting it. That difference can shape your entire life.

Let me tell you a story about two lumberjacks. They start chopping at the same time, stop at the same time, but one disappears for an hour every day and still chops more wood. His secret? He goes home to sharpen his axe. That's the infinite mindset—it's not about daily output, but lifetime output.

Simon Sinek gives us five rules. First, go after what you want without waiting in line, as long as you don't block others. Second, like Navy SEALs, the ones who make it are those who help the person next to them when they have nothing left. Third, be the last to speak like Nelson Mandela—listen to everyone first.

Fourth, sometimes you are the problem. In the 19th century, doctors didn't wash their hands and caused countless deaths, yet they blamed others. Take accountability. Fifth, stay humble and grateful—people treat you well because of your position, not you. You always deserve a styrofoam cup.

We also talked about empathy for the younger generation. They're not difficult; we've created an addictive environment. Social media, dopamine, superficial relationships—they've lost the ability to cope with stress. Loving your work is a right, not a privilege. Working hard for something you don't care about is stress; for something you love is passion.

So, how will you use these rules? Will you keep waiting in line, or go after what you want? Will you be the last to speak, or rush to share your opinion? Remember, the time you spend sharpening your axe is when you truly grow.

deconstruction.overview: 整篇演讲以「看世界的两种方式」为总纲，用五个故事和案例串起五条人生规则，最后延伸到对年轻一代的共情与热爱工作的权利。结构上先立论，再逐条展开，每条规则都用一个生动的故事或案例支撑，最后用金句收束。风格口语化、故事驱动、金句频出，善用对比和排比。

sections.title: 两种视角与无限思维
sections.argument: 看世界有两种方式：看到想要的东西，或看到阻碍。无限思维关注一生能完成什么，而非每天完成多少。
sections.evidence: 伐木工每天消失一小时却砍更多柴，因为他回家磨斧头。

sections.title: 规则一：直接去拿你想要的
sections.argument: 不必排队，可以打破常规，只要不阻挡别人。
sections.evidence: 中央公园免费百吉饼的故事：朋友只看到长队，作者直接伸手拿了两块，没人生气。

sections.title: 规则二：互相照顾
sections.argument: 成为精英战士的关键不是强壮或聪明，而是能在精疲力竭时帮助身边的人。
sections.evidence: 海豹突击队选拔：肌肉男、推卸责任的领导、明星运动员都通不过；通过的人是那些还能帮助他人的人。
sections.technique: 引用权威、列举反例、对比

sections.title: 规则三：最后一个发言
sections.argument: 像曼德拉一样，先听所有人说，再给出自己的意见，这样既让他人感到被倾听，也能获得更全面的信息。
sections.evidence: 曼德拉随父亲参加部落会议，父亲总是最后发言；董事会中过早发言会扼杀他人贡献。
sections.technique: 名人案例、场景对比、具体建议

sections.title: 规则四：承担责任
sections.argument: 有时问题出在自己身上，要像医生洗手一样，勇于承认并改正。
sections.evidence: 19世纪产褥热：医生上午解剖尸体，下午接生不洗手，导致高死亡率；霍尔姆斯指出问题却被忽视30年。
sections.technique: 历史案例、因果分析、类比

sections.title: 规则五：谦卑与感恩
sections.argument: 别人对你的优待是对你职位的，不是你本人的；永远记得自己只配一个泡沫杯。
sections.evidence: 前国防部副部长演讲：卸任后待遇从商务舱、陶瓷杯变成经济舱、泡沫杯。

sections.title: 对年轻一代的共情
sections.argument: 如果一代人挣扎，问题可能不在他们，而在我们创造的环境；要练习共情，帮助他人成为最好的自己。
sections.evidence: 社交媒体、多巴胺上瘾、表面关系、缺乏应对机制；我们问「如何榨取员工」而非「如何帮助他们」。
sections.technique: 设问、数据引用、类比、呼吁

sections.title: 热爱工作是一种权利
sections.argument: 热爱工作不是特权，而是权利；为不爱的事努力叫压力，为爱的事努力叫激情。
sections.evidence: 人们听到「我爱我的工作」会觉得像中彩票；领导者应创造让人感到安全、被关心的环境。

writing_techniques.name: 故事驱动
writing_techniques.example: 伐木工的故事、百吉饼的故事、海豹突击队的故事、曼德拉的故事、产褥热的故事、泡沫杯的故事。
writing_techniques.effect: 用具体故事承载抽象道理，让听众容易记住并产生情感共鸣。

writing_techniques.name: 对比与排比
writing_techniques.example: Some people see the thing that they want and some people see the thing that prevents them from getting the thing that they want.
writing_techniques.effect: 强化观点，制造节奏感，让语言更有冲击力。

writing_techniques.name: 设问与反问
writing_techniques.example: How do I help my people be at their natural best?
writing_techniques.effect: 引发听众思考，引导他们从被动接受转向主动反思。

writing_techniques.name: 引用权威与名人案例
writing_techniques.example: Nelson Mandela, Navy SEALs, Dr. Oliver Wendell Holmes.
writing_techniques.effect: 借助权威和名人增强说服力，让观点更具可信度。

writing_techniques.name: 金句收尾
writing_techniques.example: Working hard for something we don't care about is called stress. Working hard for something we love is called passion.
writing_techniques.effect: 用简洁有力的对比句总结全文，留下深刻印象。

actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 每天或每周固定留出一段不被打扰的时间，用于学习、反思或休息，而不是一直埋头做事。
actionable_skills.example: 每天中午花30分钟阅读行业报告或学习新技能，关掉手机和邮件。

actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 当面对一个机会但觉得「排队」太长时，思考是否有不伤害他人的替代路径，直接行动。
actionable_skills.example: 想争取一个项目，不必等轮岗，可以直接向负责人提出你的方案，只要不阻碍他人。

actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 在会议中，先记录所有人的观点，不急于表态，最后再综合给出自己的意见。
actionable_skills.example: 团队讨论时，先问每个人「你怎么看」，自己最后总结，并问「我有没有遗漏什么」。

actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 当事情出错时，先问自己「我做了什么或没做什么导致了这个结果」，而不是先怪外部。
actionable_skills.example: 项目延期，先检查自己是否及时跟进了关键节点，再讨论其他因素。

actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 把「如何让员工更努力」换成「如何帮助员工处于最佳状态」，并询问他们的真实感受。
actionable_skills.example: 一对一沟通时问：「最近工作中什么让你最有能量？什么最消耗你？」

thinking_models.explanation: 不关注短期每日产出，而关注长期一生能完成什么，愿意投资于休息和成长。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 在制定职业规划或团队目标时，问自己：这件事在五年后还重要吗？我是否在磨斧头？

thinking_models.explanation: 同一件事，有人看到目标，有人看到障碍；主动选择看到目标。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 遇到困难时，列出「我想要什么」和「我看到的障碍」，然后问：障碍是真实的还是我选择的视角？

thinking_models.explanation: 真正的领导力在于帮助身边的人，而不是证明自己多强。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 在团队中，当自己精疲力竭时，仍主动问同事「你需要什么帮助？」

thinking_models.explanation: 当一代人或一个群体出现问题时，先检查系统环境，而非指责个体。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 面对年轻员工离职率高，先分析公司文化、管理方式，而非抱怨「这代人不行」。

thinking_models.explanation: 热爱工作应是普遍权利，而非少数人的特权；领导者有责任创造这样的环境。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 在评估工作时，问自己：我是否在为自己热爱的事努力？如果不是，如何调整？

golden_sentences.sentence: Some people see the thing that they want and some people see the thing that prevents them from getting the thing that they want.
golden_sentences.why_good: 用对称结构对比两种视角，简洁有力，直击人心。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 有些人看到的是他们想要的东西，有些人看到的是阻止他们得到想要的东西的障碍。

golden_sentences.sentence: It's not about how much you can get done each day. It's how much you can get done over the course of a career or over the course of a lifetime.
golden_sentences.why_good: 对比每日与一生，强调无限思维，格局宏大。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 关键不在于你每天能完成多少，而在于你在一生或整个职业生涯中能完成多少。

golden_sentences.sentence: You don't have to wait in line. You don't have to do it the way everybody else has done it. You can do it your way. You can break the rules. You just can't get in the way of somebody else getting what they want.
golden_sentences.why_good: 排比句式，层层递进，最后一句给出边界，既有力量又有原则。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 你不必排队，不必按别人的方式做。你可以按自己的方式，可以打破规则，只是不能阻挡别人得到他们想要的。

golden_sentences.sentence: If you want to be an elite warrior, you better get really, really good at helping the person to the left of you and helping the person to the right of you.
golden_sentences.why_good: 用具体方位词「左边的人、右边的人」让抽象的领导力变得生动可感。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 如果你想成为精英战士，你最好非常非常擅长帮助左边的人和右边的人。

golden_sentences.sentence: The skill to hold your opinions to yourself until everyone has spoken.
golden_sentences.why_good: 精准概括核心技能，用「hold」一词生动表达克制。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 把意见保留到自己心里，直到所有人都说完，这是一种技能。

golden_sentences.why_good: 极简短句，直指要害，令人警醒。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 有时候，问题就出在你身上。

golden_sentences.sentence: The ceramic cup was never meant for me. It was meant for the position I held. I deserve a styrofoam cup.
golden_sentences.why_good: 用陶瓷杯和泡沫杯的对比，形象地传达谦卑，令人印象深刻。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 陶瓷杯从来不是为我准备的，而是为我所担任的职位。我只配一个泡沫杯。

golden_sentences.sentence: Working hard for something we don't care about is called stress. Working hard for something we love is called passion.
golden_sentences.why_good: 对仗工整，定义清晰，是全文的点睛之笔。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 为我们不在乎的事努力叫压力，为我们热爱的事努力叫激情。

vocabulary.context_sentence: There's a great story of two lumberjacks where every morning they start chopping wood at the same time.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 伐木工；用于描述体力劳动者或比喻埋头苦干的人。

vocabulary.context_sentence: If you take an infinite mindset, it's not about how much you can get done each day.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 无限思维；指关注长期而非短期的思考方式。

vocabulary.context_sentence: Oh, go home and sharpen my axe.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 磨斧头；比喻花时间提升自己或准备，而非一味蛮干。

vocabulary.context_sentence: The United States Navy Seals are perhaps the most elite warriors in the world.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 精英的；用于形容顶尖群体。

vocabulary.context_sentence: The pining leaders who like to delegate all their responsibility and never do anything themselves.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 委派、授权；常指把任务交给别人。

vocabulary.context_sentence: When they find themselves physically spent, emotionally spent, when they have nothing left to give.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 体力耗尽的；spent 意为用尽的。
问责、承担责任；常用于职场和个人成长。

vocabulary.context_sentence: When they started sterilizing their instruments and washing their hands, the black death of childbed disappeared.
I poured myself a cup of coffee into this here styrofoam cup.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 泡沫塑料杯；象征谦卑和普通。

vocabulary.context_sentence: This is what empathy means. It means if there's an entire generation struggling, maybe it's not them.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 共情、同理心；指理解他人感受的能力。

vocabulary.context_sentence: We know that engagement with social media and our cell phones releases a chemical called dopamine.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 多巴胺；神经递质，与快感和上瘾有关。

vocabulary.context_sentence: Because we're allowing unfettered access to these dopamine producing devices and media.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 无限制的接触；unfettered 意为不受约束的。
